result.keywords: This article examines blockchain governance and performance from a practical systems perspective, asking what measurable capabilities distributed ledger technologies provide, how those capabilities should be evaluated, and where real deployments still fall short. We synthesize evaluation metrics, survey modeling approaches, and compare application domains spanning enterprise systems, IoT integration, and public infrastructure. The goal is to distinguish design promises from operational constraints and to propose a consistent vocabulary for discussing scalability, security, and observability in blockchain-based platforms.
result.title: Blockchain Governance and Performance: Metrics, Models, and Real-World Limits
